summary: SQLite abs returns a numeric value without its sign.
documentation: SQLite abs returns a numeric value without its sign. NULL input remains NULL. For an integer input it preserves integer form when the magnitude is representable.
caution: The minimum signed 64-bit integer has no positive signed 64-bit counterpart and causes integer overflow. Tests exclude that value.
scenarios: Show the size of an invoice adjustment independently of its direction.
Measure a budget deviation from an expected integer balance.
Compare the magnitude of positive and negative stock changes.
title: Report adjustment sizes
problem: From adjustments(id INTEGER, cents INTEGER), return id and abs(cents) as magnitude for each row, ordered by id. Preserve NULL magnitudes. Inputs exclude the minimum signed 64-bit integer.
goal: Use abs() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Keep the identifier and apply abs to cents.
